summary.title: 我正在为低轨空间平台上的太阳盲紫外臭氧与高空燃烧羽流探测器设计前端滤光膜。探
summary.question: 我正在为低轨空间平台上的太阳盲紫外臭氧与高空燃烧羽流探测器设计前端滤光膜。探测器需要尽可能透过 255–280 nm 的太阳盲紫外信号，同时尽可能抑制 300–700 nm 可见光背景和 700–1100 nm 近红外杂散光。请在空气入射、熔融石英基底的条件下，设计一个不含金属层、仅使用常规可沉积无机介质材料的平面多层膜，膜系总层数不超过 30 层。

problem.compatibility_reason: Request fits planar layered media scope; no unsupported features like gratings or nonlinear optics.
manufacturing_constraints: Only conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials
ambiguities: Specific dielectric material candidates not specified

metrics.rationale: User explicitly states '尽可能透过 255–280 nm 的太阳盲紫外信号' (maximize transmission of 255-280 nm solar-blind UV signal) - this is the primary passband for the detector.
User explicitly states '尽可能抑制 300–700 nm 可见光背景' (suppress 300-700 nm visible background) - this is the first rejection band requiring high reflectance/blocking.
User explicitly states '尽可能抑制 700–1100 nm 近红外杂散光' (suppress 700-1100 nm near-infrared stray light) - this is the second rejection band requiring high reflectance/blocking.

scoring.metric_rationale: These three metrics directly map to the user's three explicit spectral requirements: one passband (255-280 nm UV transmission to maximize) and two distinct stopbands (300-700 nm visible and 700-1100 nm NIR to suppress). Using reflectance_stopband for the rejection bands is semantically appropriate per the catalogue guidance ('prefer this name for a rejection or stopband requirement'). I deliberately omit angle and polarization selectors since the user did not specify them, allowing default normal-incidence unpolarized evaluation. Manufacturing constraints (30 layers, no metals, dielectric materials only) are design variables handled by the optimizer, not scoring metrics. I use exactly 3 of the 4 allowed metrics to avoid diluting the comparison with unnecessary measures.
scoring.formula_rationale: The user phrases all three requirements with 'as much as possible' (尽可能), indicating equal priority between maximizing signal transmission and suppressing background noise. Since all metrics are normalized fractions between 0 and 1, a direct sum assigns equal weight without introducing arbitrary coefficients. This ensures that improving any single band contributes equally to the score, while failing in any band directly penalizes the total, forcing the optimization to balance passband performance with stopband blocking.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 periodic Bragg stack with single defect cavity
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A standard quarter-wave Bragg reflector pair (HfO2/SiO2) with a single half-wave defect cavity can achieve high transmission in 255-280 nm while blocking 300-1100 nm within 30 layers.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflectors create high reflectance outside the passband through constructive interference of reflections from periodic high/low index interfaces. A defect layer in the center creates a transmission resonance within the stopband.
known_risks: HfO2 may have increased absorption below 260 nm
Single cavity may not provide sharp enough passband edges
Blocking bandwidth may be insufficient for 300-1100 nm range

routes.title: HfO2-MgF2 Fabry-Perot Cavity Bandpass Filter for Solar-Blind UV
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity design with HfO2/MgF2 distributed Bragg reflectors can achieve high transmittance in 255-280 nm while suppressing 300-1100 nm, with performance improving as cavity thickness is tuned.
routes.design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Bandpass filters use high/low index pairs to create reflector stacks, with a cavity layer between them creating a transmission peak at the design wavelength. Quarter-wave optical thickness at center wavelength creates constructive interference in the passband. MgF2 has low UV absorption; HfO2 provides sufficient index contrast.

Uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal versus fewer layers with different topology - this is a recalled rule of thumb
